name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.

name: iOSWorld: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Phone Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a native iOS simulator benchmark with persistent user data, multi-app tasks, and personalization-dependent phone workflows.

name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

name: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.

name: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CausalCache, which selects archived screenshots to restore alongside text summaries under a fixed visual-memory budget. A history-gated adapter processes restored images, with evaluation distinguishing standard step limits from longer-horizon and mobile-transfer settings.

name: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. Controlled OSWorld comparisons examine both the benefits of shared procedural memory and its domain-dependent instability under repeated revision.

name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.

name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.

name: REBASE: Device-Cloud Experience Coherence for GUI Agents Across App Updates
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces REBASE, a device–cloud protocol for repairing cached GUI experience after app updates. It combines cloud replay, device-side step verification, and progressively richer failure reports to produce repairs tied to application versions.

name: PastForward: Faster On-Device GUI Agents via Computational Experience Reuse
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PastForward, which reuses earlier output sequences as verified decoding proposals and starts future action computation from predicted GUI transitions. Screen checks determine whether speculative computation and cached model states can be retained.

name: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage in Browser-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AgentTell, a benchmark for privacy leakage through browser actions after an agent learns a private fact on another website. It examines whether agents choose revealing options despite nondisclosure instructions and whether their final reports accurately describe that behavior.

name: Relevance Does Not Imply Applicability: Experience Activation for Personal GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces ExpActivator, which matches the current GUI state to relevant historical states before supplying past actions as guidance. A separate activation rule decides whether a recurring user intent is warranted by the current time and situation or should be withheld.

name: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Probe to Act, which lets browser agents request visual evidence linking DOM handles and screen regions before committing an operation. It retains selected interaction evidence as memory and studies both prompted use and distillation into open models.

name: One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Defines a test-time adaptation setting with one counted attempt per arriving GUI task and no ground-truth feedback. Its SOLO method filters or relabels completed episodes, then updates a small adapter from a short window of the agent’s own experience.

name: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes a WebRetriever agent that combines semantic webpage operations with visual localization when structured representations are insufficient. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware execution support processing tasks across concurrent browsers.

name: AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AdaptArena to test whether web agents can infer unstated user preferences from relevant past trajectories and carry those preferences into new tasks. Its AdaptiveAgent baseline separates preference-retrieval challenges from failures in downstream web execution.

name: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents PrecogUI, which retrieves prior anomaly and success patterns and predicts symbolic UI transitions before choosing actions. It also introduces InterfereBench, generated for evaluating long GUI workflows with disruptive events and recovery requirements.

name: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies repetitive, unproductive actions in desktop agents through their internal activation states. It proposes Reset, Reroute, Restore, a context intervention that temporarily resets an agent’s trajectory and later restores it to help escape repeated ineffective behavior.

name: Action Conditioned Bisimulation For GUI Agent Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Defines a GUI-memory merge rule that treats two states as equivalent only when shared actions lead to matching outcomes and successor states. The training-free method replaces observation-similarity merging and is tested in closed-loop MiniWoB++ interaction.

name: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines structured GUI exploration with training designed to tolerate imperfect retrieved experience. It builds state-transition graphs and synthetic task trajectories, then injects realistic forms of interface drift so agents learn when to rely on or reject prior guidance.

name: Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Audits WebArena-Lite outcomes and trajectories with human review to identify automatic-evaluator false negatives and the first consequential execution errors. It also studies explicit execution-state memory and procedural guidance, showing why final task scores can miss substantial differences in agent behavior.

name: Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies how to route different parts of GUI experience into model weights or runtime context rather than treating whole trajectories as a single unit. It separates locators, procedures, state facts, and lessons, then predicts their destination from recurrence and dependence on the current state.

name: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces TeleTune, which edits a textual skill library using held-out action prediction on offline software-use logs with missing goals or interleaved tasks. The learned workflows also guide retrieval of demonstrations for subsequent web-agent execution.

name: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AMBER, an append-only memory framework in which a web agent learns to reason, act, and retain evidence using outcome-reward reinforcement learning. It studies whether preserving entries avoids the loss of facts and corrective feedback seen with rewritten memory.

name: DeltaReplay: Task-Relative Memory Reuse for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces DeltaReplay, which stores mobile GUI trajectories as transition graphs and decides at each step whether to reuse an action, substitute task-specific parameters, or defer to the base agent. This supports reuse of partially matching experiences without rewriting stored memory.

name: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Web$hell, an interface that compiles live pages into persistent information and action objects so agents can gather evidence, navigate websites, and reuse acquired content through shared operations.

name: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced. Android platform tagging is additionally supported by the primary project documentation.
summary: Introduces SwitchMem, which chooses a textual or visual representation of retrieved experience at each GUI interaction step instead of fixing one memory modality for a task.

name: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CarryOn, which maintains evidence-linked task objects and remaining-work context across history compression, with evaluations on desktop tasks and web research.
